findings.claim: The public GET /groups/:name/members endpoint now defaults to limit=50 for every group, but the public route and template have no pagination controls, so members after the 50th cannot be reached.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-26 now applies `limit` (default 50) and `offset` to every group, where before only automatic groups were limited (to 200). The public route app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:8-12 calls `findMembers()` once at offset 0, and app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:1-22 has no next/previous or load-more controls (only the admin template does), so the public page cannot show members past the 50th.

findings.claim: In the group member row itemView, {{#unless automatic}} resolves against the member (Discourse.User) rather than the group, so `automatic` is undefined and the remove link is shown for automatic groups.

verifier.reason: app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:22 uses the keyword form `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, and the vendored Ember sets `hash.keyword` for that form (vendor/assets/javascripts/development/ember.js:8413) and binds the item view's context to `_parentView.context` (ember.js:7997-7998). So `automatic` in group_member.hbs:1 resolves against the admin-group controller proxying the group, not the member, and the remove link is hidden for automatic groups.

findings.claim: The item-view template references `member`, but that alias is not available inside a separate itemView template, so rows render without member data and remove can fail when the controller calls member.get(...).

verifier.reason: The loop alias is set on each item view itself, not on a block template: `EachView.createChildView` does `view._keywords[keyword] = content` (vendor/assets/javascripts/development/ember.js:8217-8225) and path lookup reads `this.view._keywords` (ember.js:38808-38809), so `member` resolves in app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1. The same pattern is already used by share.hbs:13 with share_link.hbs referencing `s`.

findings.claim: A function has code paths that end without an explicit return and return undefined.

verifier.reason: The patch changes `findMembers` at app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 from returning `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` to a bare `return ;` (undefined) while its other path returns a promise, and the new `addMembers` action at app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:61-65 falls off the end without a return. No current caller chains on these results (group.js:47,58; admin_group_route.js:13; group-members.js.es6:11), so nothing breaks today.

findings.claim: The group[usernames] parameter is now ignored by the API.

verifier.reason: After the patch, `create` and `update` in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22-47 read only top-level `params[:name]`, `params[:visible]` and `params[:alias_level]`; the removed `group.usernames = params[:group][:usernames]` / `payload[:usernames]` lines mean `group[usernames]` is silently dropped. Membership can now only be changed through the new `add_members`/`remove_member` endpoints (lines 65-97), and the PATCH `changes` path is gone too.

findings.claim: The admin group create and update actions read top-level params instead of group[...], with no compatibility path: legacy create gets a blank name (422) and legacy update silently sets visible=false.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:24-25 and :37-40 read only top-level `params[:name]`/`params[:visible]`/`params[:alias_level]` with no `params[:group]` fallback, so a legacy `group[...]` create yields name `''`, which fails `name_format_validator` (app/models/group.rb:12) and returns 422 via `render_json_error`, while a legacy update sets `visible = false`, ignores name and alias_level, and returns success. The in-repo client was updated to send top-level params (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:63-78), so only external callers using the old shape are affected.

findings.claim: GET /groups/:name/members now returns {members, meta} instead of an array, which is not backwards compatible.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28-35 now renders `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}`, where the old code called `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` and returned a bare JSON array. The in-repo caller was updated (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:25-36), but external API consumers expecting an array break, and the pending spec at spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb:78-79 still parses the body as an array.

findings.claim: The PATCH /admin/groups/:id endpoint with changes[add|delete] is removed without documentation.

verifier.reason: The patch deletes `update_patch` and the `request.patch?` dispatch, so `update` at app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34-47 no longer reads `params[:changes]`. A PATCH still routes there via `resources :groups` (config/routes.rb:45), returns success, adds or removes nobody, and resets `visible` to false at line 38; the patch adds no deprecation note, changelog or docs pointing to the new PUT/DELETE `members` routes.

findings.claim: The '== 0' comparisons at lines 7 and 12 violate the .jshintrc eqeqeq rule.

verifier.reason: `.jshintrc:61` sets `"eqeqeq": true`, and the patch adds `this.get("user_count") == 0` at `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:7` and `:12`; `eqnull` (`.jshintrc:79`) only exempts `== null`, so both lines break the rule.

findings.claim: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which gives one extra page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100/50 gives 3), so navigation can reach an empty page.

verifier.reason: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 computes totalPages as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so 100 users at limit 50 gives 3 pages instead of 2. On page 2 showingLast (line 17) is false, so next (lines 30-33) sets offset to 100 and the server (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:26) returns an empty member list shown as page 3/3.

findings.claim: The next action clamps the offset to user_count instead of the last valid offset, so it can navigate to an empty page (e.g. total equal to limit gives offset == total).

verifier.reason: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:33 clamps the next offset to `user_count`, and `totalPages` at line 13 is `floor(user_count/limit)+1`, so with 50 members and limit 50 `showingLast` is false on page 1 of 2 and `next` sets offset 50. `findMembers` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23) also clamps only to `user_count`, and the server (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:26) returns an empty member list for offset == total.

findings.claim: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), which bypasses callbacks so the groups.user_count counter_cache is not decremented, unlike add_members which uses group.add.

verifier.reason: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` on a `has_many :through` (`app/models/group.rb:8`), which in Rails 4.1.8 removes the join rows with `delete_all`, so the `counter_cache: "user_count"` on `app/models/group_user.rb:2` never decrements (Rails behaviour from memory, gem source not readable here). `add_members` goes through `group.add` (`group.rb:272`), which saves a GroupUser and increments the counter, so `user_count` from `app/serializers/basic_group_serializer.rb:2` drifts upward after removals.

findings.claim: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) instead of Group#remove, so the removed user's primary_group_id is not cleared and the group can still show as post flair.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 removes the member with `group.users.delete(user_id)`, which never reaches the only code that nulls `primary_group_id` (`destroy_deletions`, app/models/group.rb:287-292, fed only by `usernames=`, which the patch stops calling), so app/serializers/post_serializer.rb:96-103 still returns the group name as flair. One detail of the claim is wrong: `Group#remove` (group.rb:276-278) would not clear it either.

findings.claim: add_members calls usernames.split(','), assuming a string; usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b yields an Array and raises NoMethodError (500).

verifier.reason: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:67-71 takes `params.require(:usernames)` and calls `usernames.split(",")` with no type check, so `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` does end in a NoMethodError/500. The raise is one step later than the claim implies: `config/application.rb:2` loads `rails/all`, ActiveSupport 4.1.8 defines `Array#split`, so the error comes from `username.downcase` on an Array at app/models/user.rb:176.

findings.claim: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' controller spec sends xhr :put to remove_member, but the route is DELETE; it passes only because controller specs skip routing.

verifier.reason: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115 sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`, while config/routes.rb:49 declares `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (PUT maps to add_members at :50); the sibling test at spec line 125 uses `:delete`. Controller specs dispatch straight to the action without checking the HTTP verb, so the mismatch goes unnoticed (not run here).

findings.claim: The limit and offset params on the members endpoint are not validated or clamped: negative values reach SQL and cause errors, and limit has no upper cap.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-23 only apply `.to_i` to `params[:limit]` and `params[:offset]`, and line 26 passes them straight into `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no lower bound or maximum. A negative value therefore reaches PostgreSQL, which rejects negative LIMIT/OFFSET (a 500; not run here), and a very large limit returns every member.

findings.claim: findMembers() is called asynchronously without its promise being returned or awaited from setupController, so the template may render before member data is available.

verifier.reason: The patch removes the awaited `afterModel` hook and instead calls `model.findMembers()` fire-and-forget in `setupController` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:11-14 and app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:8-12), so the template does render before members load. The effect is only a brief empty list, because `findMembers` sets `members` on the model when the request resolves (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:20-37) and the bound `{{each member in members}}` then re-renders.

findings.claim: removeMember and addMembers have no rejection handler, so 422/500 responses give the admin no feedback.

verifier.reason: Both model methods chain only a success `.then` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40-60) and the controller actions discard the returned promise (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:51-65), unlike `save`/`destroy` which call `bootbox.alert` on rejection (lines 84-87, 103-105). `Discourse.ajax` only rejects the promise and shows no global error UI (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/mixins/ajax.js:51-67), so a 422 from `add_members`/`remove_member` or a 500 fails silently.

findings.claim: The usernames input is not cleared after an add operation.

verifier.reason: The `addMembers` action at app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:61-65 sends `usernames` to the model but never resets it (it even carries a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment), and `Group.addMembers` at app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:51-60 only reloads the member list.

findings.claim: add_members calls group.add(user) without checking for existing membership, so adding an existing member violates the unique index on group_users(group_id,user_id) and raises RecordNotUnique (500), and earlier users stay committed because there is no transaction.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71-75 loops `group.add(user)` with no membership check or transaction; `Group#add` (app/models/group.rb:272-274) is `self.users.push(user)` on a persisted has_many :through, which inserts each join row immediately, and GroupUser has no uniqueness validation while db/migrate/20130416004933_group_users.rb:9 puts a unique index on (group_id,user_id). The resulting RecordNotUnique is only logged and re-raised (app/controllers/application_controller.rb:62-74), so the request 500s after earlier users are already committed.

findings.claim: Removing the last member on the last page leaves an empty page because findMembers keeps the old offset.

verifier.reason: After a delete, `removeMember` calls `findMembers` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40-48), which re-sends the old offset clamped only to the stale `user_count` (group.js:23); with 51 members on page 2 it requests offset 50, and the server echoes that offset with zero rows (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-34), so the list is empty and the pager stays on page 2.

findings.claim: The pending 'ensures that membership can be paginated' spec still parses the old array shape, and no spec covers the new {members, meta} response contract.

verifier.reason: The patch changes `GroupsController#members` to return `{members: [...], meta: {...}}` (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28-35), but the pending spec at spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb:72-85 still does `JSON.parse(response.body)` and maps `m['username']` over the result as if it were an array. No file under spec/ or test/ references the `members`/`meta` keys or `findMembers`, so the new contract is unasserted.

findings.claim: group.save with render_json_error after add/remove is effectively a no-op, because membership writes already hit the DB via has_many :through, so the error branch only fires on unrelated group validation failures.

verifier.reason: Both actions load a persisted group with `Group.find` (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:66,85), so `group.add` → `self.users.push(user)` (app/models/group.rb:272-274) and `group.users.delete(user_id)` (groups_controller.rb:90) write the `group_users` join rows immediately under Rails 4.1.8. `GroupUser` has no validations (app/models/group_user.rb:1-4), so the following `group.save` (groups_controller.rb:77,92) changes no attributes and can only fail on the group's own name/alias_level validations (group.rb:12-13,37).

findings.claim: addMembers ends with '})' without a semicolon, which triggers jshint W033 under .jshintrc.

verifier.reason: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:59 ends the `return Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` statement with `})` and no semicolon (the sibling removeMember at line 48 has one). .jshintrc does not set `asi`, and `lastsemic: true` (line 81) only exempts a missing semicolon when the closing brace is on the same line, which is not the case here, so W033 applies; the file is not in .jshintignore. Not run through jshint here, judged from the config.

findings.claim: There is a stray semicolon after a block (if (!this.get('id')) { return };), which triggers jshint W032.

verifier.reason: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:82 reads `if (!this.get('id')) { return };`, added by the patch in the new `destroy` method; the semicolon after the closing brace is an empty statement (jshint W032), and .jshintrc does not suppress it (only `lastsemic` is set, at .jshintrc:81). I did not run jshint.

findings.claim: The routes provide the group id in params[:id], but the controller reads params[:group_id], causing a param-missing failure.

verifier.reason: The new routes at config/routes.rb:49-50 sit directly inside `resources :groups do ... end`, not in a `member do` block, so Rails generates `/admin/groups/:group_id/members` and supplies params[:group_id]. That matches `params.require(:group_id)` in add_members and remove_member in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb; the non-admin `get 'members'` route at config/routes.rb:271-272 uses the same pattern with `find_group(:group_id)`.

findings.claim: The Group#usernames= setter, destroy_deletions and after_save :destroy_deletions are now dead code in production; only specs call the setter.

verifier.reason: The patch removes the only production callers of `group.usernames =` (the old `update_put` and `create` in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb); the remaining callers are spec/models/group_spec.rb:149,153 and spec/models/user_spec.rb:1011,1022. `@deletions` is set only in that setter (app/models/group.rb:257), so the `after_save :destroy_deletions` hook (group.rb:10, 287-295) still fires on every save but never does anything in production.

findings.claim: The create action never reads params[:alias_level], although the form sends it, so the value is dropped on create.

verifier.reason: `create` at app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22-32 sets only `name` and `visible`, while `update` at line 37 does read `params[:alias_level]`; the client's `create()` posts `asJSON()`, which includes `alias_level` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js, per the patch), so the value is dropped on create. The pre-patch `create` also ignored it, but the patch rewrote the action and kept the omission.

findings.claim: add_members does not normalize usernames before lookup, so whitespace or blank entries cause valid users to be skipped.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71-72 does `usernames.split(",")` with no strip, and `User.find_by_username` (app/models/user.rb:175-176) only downcases, so "alice, bob" silently skips bob while still returning success. Blank entries are harmless (they just match nobody), and the UI joins with a bare "," (user-selector.js.es6:52), so only the whitespace half holds and only for direct API callers.

findings.claim: The group/members.hbs template contains a stray closing tag with no matching opening tag.

verifier.reason:
app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:19 has a `` after the closing `` with no opening `
` anywhere in the file. The patch only changed line 6 (`{{#each m in model}}` to `{{#each m in members}}`), so the stray tag is pre-existing.

findings.claim: The SCSS hardcodes the colors #333 and #aaa instead of using SCSS variables.

verifier.reason: The patch adds `color: #333 !important;` and `color: #aaa !important;` for `.next, .previous` at app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:472 and :474, while the rest of the file uses theme variables such as `$primary` and `scale-color(...)` (e.g. lines 29, 275).

findings.claim: The guard in group/members.hbs checks model, but the loop iterates over members, so the table header can render with no rows.

verifier.reason: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:1 still guards on `{{#if model}}` while line 6 now loops `{{#each m in members}}`; routes/group-members.js.es6:10-11 sets model to the group object (always truthy) and loads members asynchronously without waiting, so the header row renders with no rows for an empty group or while loading.

findings.claim: findMembers builds its URL from the bound, possibly unsaved group name, so after the name is edited, paging/add/remove request /groups/<unsaved-name>/members.json and get a 404.

verifier.reason: `findMembers` builds its URL from `this.get('name')` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:25), and that name is two-way bound to the edit field (app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:8), so paging and the post-add/remove reloads (group.js:47,58; admin-group.js.es6:37,48) request `/groups/<unsaved-name>/members.json` and fail. Two details differ from the claim: the failure is a 403 rather than a 404, since `ensure_can_see!(nil)` raises InvalidAccess (lib/guardian/ensure_magic.rb:18-19), and the add/remove requests themselves go by id and succeed — only the member-list reload breaks.

findings.claim: The commit body is empty, contrary to CONTRIBUTING §5's requirement to describe breaking changes.

verifier.reason: The patch file is a bare diff with no commit message, and the git metadata directory is not readable here, so whether the commit body is empty cannot be checked. CONTRIBUTING.md:59-63 does ask for a summary line plus detailed description, but says nothing specific about breaking changes.

findings.claim: The offset is clamped in the next/previous actions and again in findMembers.

verifier.reason: The `next` action clamps the offset to `user_count` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:33) and `previous` clamps it to 0 (same file, line 44); `findMembers` then clamps the same offset to [0, user_count] again (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23). The duplication is redundant but harmless.
